From 356b57752c91cffb35356abe6647065bf0edcad1 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: "Rafael J. Wysocki" <rafael.j.wysocki@intel.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Feb 2018 12:10:59 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] platform/x86: intel-hid: Reset wakeup capable flag on removal

The intel-hid device will not be able to wake up the system any more
after removing the notify handler provided by its driver, so make
its sysfs attributes reflect that.

Fixes: ef884112e55c (platform: x86: intel-hid: Wake up the system from suspend-to-idle)
Signed-off-by: Rafael J. Wysocki <rafael.j.wysocki@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Andy Shevchenko <andriy.shevchenko@linux.intel.com>

diff --git a/drivers/platform/x86/intel-hid.c b/drivers/platform/x86/intel-hid.c
index d1a01311c1a2..5e3df194723e 100644
--- a/drivers/platform/x86/intel-hid.c
+++ b/drivers/platform/x86/intel-hid.c
@@ -376,6 +376,7 @@ static int intel_hid_remove(struct platform_device *device)
 {
 	acpi_handle handle = ACPI_HANDLE(&device->dev);
 
+	device_init_wakeup(&device->dev, false);
 	acpi_remove_notify_handler(handle, ACPI_DEVICE_NOTIFY, notify_handler);
 	intel_hid_set_enable(&device->dev, false);
 	intel_button_array_enable(&device->dev, false);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/platform/x86/intel-hid.c`**
   - A new line was added in the `intel_hid_remove` function:
     ```c
     device_init_wakeup(&device->dev, false);
     ```
   - This line resets the wakeup capable flag for the `intel-hid` device to `false` when the device is removed.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modification in `intel-hid.c` is directly related to the functionality of the `intel-hid` device in terms of power management. By resetting the wakeup capable flag to `false`, the patch ensures that the device will not be able to wake the system from suspend after its removal. This change addresses a potential issue where the device might still be incorrectly reported as capable of waking the system, which could lead to unexpected behavior. The patch is a fix for a previous commit that enabled the device to wake the system, ensuring that the system's state accurately reflects the device's current capabilities.

Here is the commit message:
platform/x86: intel-hid: Reset wakeup capable flag on removal

The intel-hid device will not be able to wake up the system any more
after removing the notify handler provided by its driver, so make
its sysfs attributes reflect that.

Fixes: ef884112e55c (platform: x86: intel-hid: Wake up the system from suspend-to-idle)
Signed-off-by: Rafael J. Wysocki <rafael.j.wysocki@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Andy Shevchenko <andriy.shevchenko@linux.intel.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug arises from the failure to reset the wakeup capable flag for the `intel-hid` device when it is removed. This oversight can lead to the system incorrectly believing that the device can still wake it from suspend, resulting in unexpected behavior after the device has been detached.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int intel_hid_remove(struct platform_device *device)
 {
 	acpi_handle handle = ACPI_HANDLE(&device->dev);
 
+	device_init_wakeup(&device->dev, false);
 	acpi_remove_notify_handler(handle, ACPI_DEVICE_NOTIFY, notify_handler);
 	intel_hid_set_enable(&device->dev, false);
 	intel_button_array_enable(&device->dev, false);
 
 	/*
 	 * Even if we failed to shut off the event stream, we can still
 	 * safely detach from the device.
 	 */
 	return 0;
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
acpi_remove_notify_handler(handle, ACPI_DEVICE_NOTIFY, notify_handler);
intel_hid_set_enable(&device->dev, false);
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because the `intel-hid` device does not reset its wakeup capable flag when it is removed. The removal of the notify handler and disabling the device does not update the system's understanding of the device's ability to wake it from suspend, leading to incorrect behavior.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
device_init_wakeup(&device->dev, false);
```
Reason:
This statement explicitly resets the wakeup capable flag for the `intel-hid` device to `false` when the device is removed. This ensures that the system correctly reflects the device's inability to wake it from suspend, preventing unexpected behavior after the device has been detached.
